title: Zyxel fixes zero-day exploited to hack nearly 1,000 network switches
summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a severe security flaw in Zyxel network switches to steal sensitive files and take control of devices. Even though the maker tried to fix it, researchers found the first patch failed, requiring users to install a newly released update.

also_covered.title: Zyxel GS1900 Patch Fails to Block Zero-Day Exploit Allowing Root Command Execution

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your home or workplace uses Zyxel GS1900 network switches, your IT or network team needs to update the device software immediately.
action_it: Apply the new firmware update released by Zyxel for the affected GS1900 models, as the previous 2.90 fix was incomplete and left devices vulnerable to root command execution.

title: Hackers backdoor Linux servers using trojanized CWP web server
summary: Hackers are distributing malicious software disguised as a legitimate web server used for managing Linux systems. This allows attackers to secretly control compromised servers.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you manage a server using Control Web Panel, check your systems immediately.
action_it: Inspect servers running Control Web Panel for unauthorized modifications to the cwpsrv web server and monitor systems for signs of the CWPdoor malware.

title: DigiCert data breach exposes customer information, identity documents
summary: DigiCert suffered a data breach after a server migration accidentally exposed an internal system to the internet. This allowed unauthorized access to customer details and identity documents.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you are a DigiCert customer, watch out for official communications from the company regarding your account and identity documents.
action_it: Review internal server configurations and migration processes to ensure no other internal business systems are exposed to the internet. Monitor affected systems for signs of unauthorized access.

title: DreamHost confirms data breach exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions
summary: DreamHost confirmed that attackers accessed its File Manager platform for two months and stole customers' FTP and SFTP login credentials. This matters because stolen logins can allow unauthorized access to customer websites and files.

also_covered.title: ThreatsDay: Apache OFBiz RCE, DreamHost Breach, DeFi Site Hijacks + 17 More Stories

action_everyone: If you are a DreamHost customer, you should immediately change your FTP, SFTP, and webmail passwords, and check your accounts for any unauthorized activity.

title: Hackers Exploit Patched Apple Flaw to Deliver Info-Stealing Malware, CISA Says
summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a security flaw in Apple operating systems to deliver malware that steals personal information. Users and administrators need to ensure their Apple devices are updated to protect against these attacks.
action_everyone: Check your Apple device settings and install the latest software updates available today to protect against this flaw.
action_it: Review systems for exposure to CVE-2024-27834 and ensure all affected Apple operating systems are updated with the latest patches provided by Apple.

title: Closing the Identity Gap at the Service Desk
summary: Cybercriminals are tricking IT help desks into resetting passwords and registering new login devices to bypass security checks. Organizations need stronger identity verification to stop these social engineering attacks.

title: GhostMap Android flaw lets malicious app trigger persistent boot loop
summary: A newly discovered Android flaw allows malicious apps to force devices into an endless restart loop requiring no special permissions. This matters because a simple app installation can render a phone unusable until it is factory reset.

title: Cyberattack disrupts blood storage refrigeration systems in France
summary: A cyberattack hit a refrigeration equipment supplier in France, altering temperatures at three national blood service facilities. This incident threatened the safety of stored blood products.

title: Is Your Exposure Management Platform Leaving You Exposed? Five Tests to Find Out
summary: An analysis highlights gaps in exposure management tools where security findings lack crucial context needed for remediation. This matters because organizations may remain vulnerable even after a security ticket is generated.

title: OpenAI AI Pipeline Generates 948 Linux Root Escalation Exploits in 30-Hour Run
summary: OpenAI used an upcoming cyber-focused AI model to find, validate, and patch nearly a thousand Linux security flaws over a 30-hour run. This research demonstrates how artificial intelligence can be used to rapidly discover and exploit software weaknesses at scale.

title: 5 Active Cyber Threats That Put US Enterprises at Risk in October 2026
summary: A security report outlines five active cyber threats targeting U.S. enterprises in October 2026. These campaigns exploit trusted platforms and everyday workflows to cause financial and operational harm.

title: Apple to Start Scanning Publicly Shared iCloud Photos and Files for Harmful Content
summary: Apple plans to start scanning publicly shared iCloud photos and files for harmful content starting in upcoming software updates. This change only affects files and photos that users explicitly share by creating a link accessible to anyone.

Vercel rolls out new protection against stolen session cookie attacks
summary: Vercel is introducing a new security feature called Device Bound Session Credentials to protect against malware that steals login sessions. This update helps prevent attackers from misusing stolen cookies to access user accounts.
